title: DJ firmware faults by version, AlphaTheta and Pioneer DJ
description: Every fault AlphaTheta document in a firmware change history, per model, with the version that fixed it and the version at or above which the model carries none of them. Faults only; feature additions are left out.
terms: Licensed CC BY 4.0: free to reuse, quote and redistribute, with credit to Save My Gig and a link to https://www.savemygig.com/knowledge/pioneer-dj/firmware. Every row names the AlphaTheta document it rests on.

fields.safeFloor: lowest version at or above which every documented fault below is fixed; null when nothing is documented
fields.withdrawn: a version above the safe floor that AlphaTheta withdrew; do not install it
fields.midSet: our marker, not AlphaTheta's: the documented symptom can interrupt a set in progress

models.note: A young unit. AlphaTheta has published no defect fix for it, so there is nothing to report here. This section stays empty until a documented one exists.

withdrawn.text: Withdrawn by AlphaTheta. It added OneLibrary, then playlists failed to display for people exporting from older rekordbox. No music or data was deleted, and the player reverted to Device Library. Do not install this version.

models.note: AlphaTheta publish a long record for this player, twelve dated versions from December 2009 to 4.33 in February 2015, and nothing since. Only the entries that name a defect appear in the table above; the feature releases and the sound-quality improvements are on the model page.

AlphaTheta publish one entry for this player, 1.10 of 2 July 2026, and it names no defect: it added compatibility with Serato DJ Pro and djay Pro, and closes with "Other minor bugs have been fixed." Below 1.10 neither of those applications will control the deck, which is the one thing the record does tell you.

models.note: Ver. 3.21 is the highest published version and AlphaTheta render its date two ways on their own material, 10 July 2018 in the change history and 7 October 2018 on the article, which is the ordinary 07/10 ambiguity. Ver. 3.20 added KUVO support and 3.18 improved SIDECHAIN REMIX and added manual effects to it, both additions rather than named defects, so neither carries a row. THE HISTORY HAS NO VERSION BELOW 3.18, and that is the answer to the DJM-2000 question rather than a gap: 3.18 is where the two products converged. The DJM-2000 is a different product with its own history and it has no row here because this site has no page for it. The two share a firmware filename from 3.18 onward and that is not permission to flash either machine with the other file.

This deck is fully analog with no digital control path. The AlphaTheta Help Center product page for it carries no Firmware section, unlike the PLX-CRSS12 page, and the manual makes no mention of firmware anywhere. There is nothing to publish and nothing to update.

models.note: Ver. 1.05 of 9 March 2021 is the highest published version and its entire published note is that minor issues were fixed, so it carries no row. It does carry a documented consequence, printed by AlphaTheta on the firmware article itself: after updating to 1.05 the Sampler Master Volume in Serato DJ Pro no longer syncs with the SAMPLER VOL knob, and the level has to be set in software instead. Version 1.02 had already changed that knob’s MIDI message. Versions 1.00, 1.01, 1.03 and 1.04 are implied by the numbering and AlphaTheta’s change history document refused every request during research, so nothing is claimed about them.

models.note: Ver. 1.02 of 06/Feb/2020 is the current and only published version. AlphaTheta show its changes and no earlier change history could be found, so nothing is claimed about 1.00 or 1.01. models.note: Ver. 1.07 is the end of the record and AlphaTheta say so themselves: if the unit reads 1.07 there is nothing to update. Two dates exist for it, 13 May 2013 in the change history document and 06/Feb/2020 on the article, and the 2013 date is the contemporaneous one. THE UPDATER NEEDS JAVA, which AlphaTheta state in one line and which is the reason an update appears to do nothing on a machine with no Java runtime installed. After updating, the change history advises recalibrating the touch sensor levels.

AlphaTheta publish no firmware download and no version history for this model at all. Its product page has no Firmware Update section, which was verified by fetching the page and enumerating all seven of its sections, and every former pioneerdj.com firmware path redirects away. That is an absence of publishing and not an absence of firmware: AlphaTheta’s own troubleshooting tells you to read the version out of the DDJ-SR2 Setting Utility. Nothing is listed here because nothing is published, and a version you cannot compare against anything is a version you cannot act on.

models.note: Ver. 1.10 of 27 June 2019 is the highest published version. Ver. 1.08 improved tempo slider accuracy, which is an improvement rather than a named defect and carries no row. Versions 1.00 to 1.03, 1.06 and 1.07 are absent from the published change history and nothing is claimed about them. A version 1.11 is claimed by a third party and AlphaTheta’s own page and change history both stop at 1.10, so it is not published here as fact. Firmware for this model ships as a Windows package only.

Only one official firmware release is published, 1.02, which added Algoriddim djay support for Android. No documented defect fix exists yet. If it behaves strangely, the answer is almost never a missing update.

models.note: The published history holds six versions and three of them name a defect. The other three are additions and carry no row by the same rule every entry here follows: 1.10 extended the maximum sample length to 64 seconds and added project file loading, 1.20 raised the PRO DJ LINK ceiling to six units with CDJ-3000s and added Drum Machine mode, and 1.22 of 7 November 2024 changed the automatic shut off time to 20 minutes to comply with the EU Ecodesign Directive. Version 1.21 does not appear in the record. 1.20 is the version that matters most in a booth even though it fixed nothing.
